module_title: High Courts - Independence, Common HCs, and Judicial Review
introduction: This advanced level explores the constitutional safeguards for the independence of the High Court, the nuances of Common High Courts, and the evolution of the power of Judicial Review as part of the basic structure.

core_concepts.title: Independence of High Court
core_concepts.description: To ensure impartial justice, the Constitution provides: 1. Security of tenure. 2. Fixed service conditions. 3. Expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund. 4. Ban on practice after retirement (except in SC or other HCs). 5. Freedom to appoint its staff.

core_concepts.title: Common High Courts
core_concepts.description: The Parliament has the power to establish a common High Court. Examples: 1. Gauhati HC (Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Arunachal). 2. Bombay HC (Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Daman & Diu). 3. Punjab and Haryana HC (Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh).

core_concepts.title: Power of Judicial Review
core_concepts.description: High Courts can examine the constitutionality of both central and state laws. If a law violates the Constitution, the HC can declare it ultra vires (null and void). In the L. Chandra Kumar Case (1997), the SC declared this power as part of the 'Basic Structure'.

core_concepts.title: Transfer of Judges (Article 222)
core_concepts.description: The President can transfer a judge from one High Court to another after consulting the Chief Justice of India. The CJI's opinion in this matter is binding and requires consultation with four senior-most judges of the SC.

important_entities.name: L. Chandra Kumar Case (1997)
important_entities.significance: The Supreme Court ruled that the power of judicial review over legislative action vested in the High Courts under Article 226 is an integral and essential feature of the Constitution.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: High Courts can strike down NOT ONLY state laws but also Central laws (Acts of Parliament) if they violate the Constitution.
This is a frequent 'Statement-based' trap: Salaries are from the STATE fund, but Pensions are from the CENTRAL fund (Consolidated Fund of India).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Arunachal, Nagaland, Assam, Mizoram. These are the four states currently served by the Gauhati High Court.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Assertion-Reasoning questions, perfectly align the 'Independence of Judiciary' with the 'Basic Structure' doctrine.
Pay close attention to the list of Union Territories and which High Court has jurisdiction over them (e.g., Lakshadweep falls under Kerala HC, Andaman & Nicobar under Calcutta HC).
